levels.2: Limited, ending or letter of intent

summary.title: European governments have spent at least €1.4 billion on Palantir
summary.detail: Follow the Money investigation. The real figure is higher because some governments, including the Netherlands and Sweden, would not say. The UK accounts for about €1.17 billion.

summary.title: Global week of action against Palantir
summary.detail: Protests on several continents over Palantir's work with the Israeli military and US immigration enforcement.

international.title: NATO: Maven Smart System
international.detail: Allied Command Operations (SHAPE, Mons, Belgium) acquired Palantir's AI battlefield system.

international.title: Europol: Gotham via Capgemini
international.detail: EU police agency analysis platform, about €7.5 million.

international.title: MEPs question the European Commission about Palantir
international.detail: Members of the European Parliament raised questions about Palantir's role in Europe.

items.title: US Army enterprise agreement
items.detail: Up to $10 billion over 10 years, consolidating Army software contracts.

items.title: Maven Smart System expansion
items.detail: Reported $618 million expansion of the Army's AI targeting and battlefield-data platform.

items.title: Department of Homeland Security blanket purchase agreement
items.detail: Five-year agreement worth up to $1 billion for AI and data analytics, paid through task orders.

items.title: USDA food-supply deal
items.detail: $300 million deal with the Department of Agriculture to manage farmland and supply-chain risk.

items.title: ICE: ImmigrationOS
items.detail: About $30 million platform to track and prioritise people for deportation.

items.title: Treasury common API layer
items.detail: Developer platform, workflow automation and data analytics for the Treasury.

items.title: IRS 'mega API' and tax data
items.detail: Senators Wyden and Markey and Rep. Ocasio-Cortez demanded answers over Palantir helping DOGE build a searchable database linking tax data with other records, saying it likely breaks the Privacy Act and tax privacy laws.

items.title: ICE 'ELITE' tool uses Medicaid data
items.detail: Reported tool that pulls Medicaid and other government data to build dossiers and arrest leads. Criticised by the EFF and KFF.

items.title: IRS contracts under scrutiny
items.detail: Tax Notes reports scrutiny of Palantir's IRS contracts amid the tax-data controversy.

items.title: Palantir wins lawsuit against the US Army
items.detail: Court of Federal Claims ruled the Army broke a 1994 procurement law by not considering commercial software. Palantir later won a major Army contract.

items.title: Sued by San Antonio defence contractor
items.detail: Guardian Premier Solutions alleges fraud and breach of contract over a $709,000 'partnership program'.

items.title: Shareholder lawsuits dismissed
items.detail: Securities and derivative suits against Palantir executives were dismissed in April 2025; one was appealed to the Tenth Circuit.

items.title: Presbyterian Church (USA) divests
items.detail: Voted unanimously to sell about $2.5 million of Palantir stock.

items.title: University of San Francisco divests
items.detail: Divested from defence companies including Palantir after student protests.

items.title: Ministry of Defence enterprise agreement
items.detail: Since 2020; enterprise agreement Dec 2022; new deal of about £240 million in Dec 2025. UK deals total about £992 million.

items.title: NHS England Federated Data Platform
items.detail: £330 million contract envelope to link hospital data.

items.title: Financial Conduct Authority
items.detail: £30,000 a month to analyse sensitive FCA data.

items.title: Home Office firearms licensing
items.detail: About £9 million replacement system.

items.title: AWE Nuclear Security Technologies
items.detail: About £15 million via Crown Commercial Service.

items.title: Cabinet Office 'Border Flow'
items.detail: Brexit border data platform.

items.title: Foxglove legal challenge to NHS deal
items.detail: Foxglove, Doctors' Association UK, National Pensioners Convention and Just Treatment argued the data platform had no legal basis.

items.title: Good Law Project sues over redacted NHS contract
items.detail: 417 of 586 contract pages were blanked out.

items.title: MPs urge ending NHS contract
items.detail: Cross-party Health and Social Care Committee urged ministers to consider ending the contract; NHS England's chief questioned its benefit assessments (8 July 2026).

items.title: Met Police deal blocked, Palantir sues, then settles
items.detail: London's Mayor's Office blocked a ~£50 million Met Police AI deal in May 2026. Palantir sued in June; both sides settled on 14 Oct 2026 and Palantir was let back into bidding.

items.title: Commons debate on MoD Palantir contracts
items.detail: Ministry of Defence Palantir contracts debated in Parliament.

items.title: Council pension investments criticised
items.detail: A Labour council's Palantir investments rose 1,200% during the Gaza war, Novara Media reports.

items.title: Ministry of Digital Transformation
items.detail: Foundry/AIP; started June 2022, MoU May 2023.

items.title: Ministry of Defence and Armed Forces
items.detail: Battlefield data and targeting support.

items.title: Brave1 Dataroom
items.detail: Defence-tech data room on Foundry.

items.title: Hesse police 'HessenDATA'
items.detail: Gotham crime analysis.

items.title: North Rhine-Westphalia police 'DAR'
items.detail: About €14 million.

items.title: Bavaria police 'VeRA'
items.detail: Went live 25 Dec 2024.

items.title: Baden-Württemberg police
items.detail: Five-year deal of about €25 million signed before there was a legal basis; Greens and CDU later agreed to change the police law to allow it.

items.title: Constitutional Court ruling
items.detail: Use of Palantir-based automated analysis in Hesse and Hamburg ruled unconstitutional after a case by the GFF civil-rights group.

items.title: Federal government reviews nationwide use
items.detail: Interior Minister Dobrindt examined using Palantir for federal police; SPD and Greens opposed. No final decision reported.

items.title: Bundeswehr procurement not awarded to Palantir
items.detail: Armed forces chose not to award a procurement to Palantir.

items.title: DGSI domestic intelligence
items.detail: Gotham since 2016 for counter-terrorism; renewed Dec 2025.

items.title: Switch to French supplier ChapsVision
items.detail: DGSI to replace Palantir, citing sovereignty concerns.

items.title: National police 'POL-INTEL'
items.detail: Gotham; Danish police have paid about €28 million.

items.title: Security and Intelligence Service 'PET-INTEL'
items.detail: Gotham.

items.title: Defence contract
items.detail: Denmark is one of eight European countries with Palantir defence deals.

items.title: Plans to seek local alternatives
items.detail: Denmark announced it will look for alternatives to Palantir.

items.title: Ministry of Defence
items.detail: In use since 2010. Government would not disclose spending.

items.title: National Police
items.detail: Deployment since 2012; current status unclear.

items.title: European alternative within two years
items.detail: Government said a full alternative to Palantir must be ready within two years.

items.title: Pension fund ABP divests
items.detail: The Dutch civil-service pension fund sold its Palantir stake.

items.title: Armed Forces Intelligence Center (CIFAS)
items.detail: About €16.5 million; reportedly expires Nov 2026.

items.title: State companies told not to sign or renew
items.detail: Reported instruction to state-controlled firms (including Telefónica, Indra, Navantia) not to sign new or renewed Palantir contracts.

items.title: Ministry of Defence
items.detail: About €6.2 million.

items.title: Defence contract
items.detail: Sweden has a Palantir defence deal but would not disclose spending.

items.title: Defence contract
items.detail: One of eight European countries with Palantir defence deals.

items.title: Norwegian Customs
items.detail: Gotham passenger and vehicle screening since 2017; extended to 2030 with an option to 2035.

items.title: Norwegian Police
items.detail: Police and customs have paid about €52 million in total. Reports conflict: one says a police system was cancelled in 2020 after ~NOK 100 million, another that police won't renew when the contract ends in 2027.

items.title: Amnesty Norway criticises customs deal
items.detail: Customs extended the contract despite criticism.

items.title: Storebrand divests
items.detail: Norway's largest asset manager sold its ~$24 million stake over Palantir's work in the occupied Palestinian territories.

items.title: COVID-19 crisis centre
items.detail: Foundry hosted on AWS.

items.title: Ministry of National Defence letter of intent
items.detail: Letter of intent only, no contract reported.

items.title: Ministry of National Defence big-data hub
items.detail: Strategic partnership from 2023; contracts could exceed €67 million by 2031.

items.title: Ministry of Defence strategic partnership
items.detail: Partnership to support Israel's war effort, agreed at a Palantir board meeting held in Israel.

items.title: Global protests and divestment over Gaza
items.detail: Campaigns call on institutions to cut ties with Palantir over its Israeli military work.

items.title: Department of Defence
items.detail: $7.6 million one-year contract (limited tender); Defence has spent over $26 million with Palantir since 2013, and Palantir staff work inside the department.

items.title: ASD, ACIC and AUSTRAC
items.detail: Contracts with the Signals Directorate, Criminal Intelligence Commission and financial-intelligence agency.

items.title: Greens campaign to cancel contracts
items.detail: The Australian Greens are campaigning to end Palantir's government contracts.

items.title: Turned down at least nine times
items.detail: Swiss federal agencies rejected Palantir repeatedly over seven years, citing no need or reputational risk.

items.title: Palantir sues magazine Republik
items.detail: Palantir sued over Republik's reporting; one report says Palantir lost on 22 of 23 claims (unconfirmed).

items.title: Defence ministry deal fell through
items.detail: Deal failed despite a 2018 pilot.
